identity_evidence.quote: A 63-year-old male with a pertinent past medical history of mitral regurgitation

attribution_limitations: The abstract and introduction attribute the endocarditis to vigorous flossing ("secondary to vigorous flossing", "flossing-induced"); this is the authors' causal claim for the case, not a tested mechanism, so no cause is recorded on the diagnosis. Do not infer other portals of entry were excluded beyond the denied dental work and procedures.

Route is stated once ("intravenously") after both vancomycin and piperacillin/tazobactam and once ("IV") for gentamicin; no route is stated for penicillin G, so none is recorded. Outpatient infusion courses at discharge are recorded with unknown action because the source does not state they were completed.

claims.text: Initial vitals, electrocardiogram and chest radiograph were normal. White blood cell count was 10,100 cells/uL with an elevated C-reactive protein of 14.00 mg/dL and erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 95 mm/h; complete metabolic panel, urinalysis and thyroid stimulating hormone were within normal limits. Three blood cultures grew Gram-positive cocci speciated to Streptococcus gordonii. After an unremarkable transthoracic echocardiogram, transesophageal echocardiography showed a small vegetation on the posterior leaflet of the mitral valve; the case is reported as subacute S. gordonii infective endocarditis on a native mitral valve.
